en: Udāna 2.7 Ekaputtakasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower had lost his only son, who was dear and beloved to him.
Then a number of lay followers, with their clothes wet and their hair wet, approached the Blessed One during the very day.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
As those lay followers were sitting there, the Blessed One said this to them:
"Lay followers, why have you come here in the middle of the day with your clothes wet and your hair wet?"
When this was said, that lay follower said to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, my only son, dear and beloved, has passed away.
Because of that, we have come here in the middle of the day with our clothes wet and our hair wet."
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Both the various hosts of devas and human beings are bound by their attachment to the gratification of what is pleasant.”
Those who are sinful and have wasted their lives fall under the power of King Māra— those who,
indeed, [neglect the Dhamma] by day and by night.
The heedful abandon that which is dear to them;
they indeed dig out the root of evil,
the bait of Death so difficult to escape.
